title: Usaunny Jump
text: Before I knew it, I found myself back at the island’s entrance, as if I’d been transported by a portal.
“Made it back, huh.”
“The trip back was instant.”
“The island looks… lively with all the activity, but nothing seems wrong.”
“So the whole-humanity-turns-into-cultivation-creatures scenario was averted, was it…”
“Why do you sound a little disappointed?”
Itsuki said this in a somewhat wistful tone.
“No, it’s just that a future where everyone became cultivation creatures might, in a certain sense, mean the end of racial discrimination, I thought.”
Father and Ren furrowed their brows at Itsuki’s answer.
“I’m sure discrimination would still happen. Like the Peckul, Usaunny, Inult, and Riska races each fighting for supremacy or whatever.”
“Probably. Not unless everyone’s got the airheaded optimism of a Filolial.”
“Some Filolial-sama are quite clever, I say!”
Calling them airheaded is harsh, indeed. They simply express through action the wonder of moving forward guided by rich sensitivity rather than deep thought.
“Is that how it works, I wonder…”
“Ah, it’s the heroes over there!”
Fiancée spotted us returning, together with Sakura. Almost at the same moment, Rival came swooping down from the sky.
“Nano, felt something off in the flow of magic power, so nano came to check it out.”
“Sakura-chan, Melty-chan, Gaelion-chan, we’re back.”
“Naofumi, welcome back~”
“Where’s Yuki-chan, I wonder?”
“Waiting at the dungeon entrance for Spear Hero to return, nano. Nano will call her right away, so don’t worry, nano.”
Rival’s testimony can hardly be trusted, indeed. I glanced at Fiancée, who let out a sigh and called over to one of the island staff. It seemed Yuki-chan and the others would be arriving shortly.
“So, heroes, still in those forms means… the results weren’t good, nano?”
“No, that’s not it—we did clear the dungeon, but right at the end we found what seems like a hint for turning back to normal.”
“I was a little worried, but I’m glad you’re all safe.”
Fiancée let out a relieved sigh, hand on her chest.
“I see, that’s good, nano. So what’s next, nano?”
“Honestly, I think what comes next is only going to end up as a joke.”
“Yeah.”
“What kind of hint, nano?”
“Ah, well, actually—”
And so Father and the others explained to Rival about the mural we’d seen earlier.
“The island’s monument… when Gaelion saw it too, nano thought Naofumi would probably be thinking exactly this, nano.”
“Having watched Naofumi-san for so many years, you can read him like a book, Gaelion-san?”
“Wild Naofumi and gentle Naofumi, both think the same things when they’re spacing out, nano~”
Ugh… even I knew that much, indeed! And Big Sister always catches on just as fast, pointing it out before I even can! Even in her adult form, mind you.
“Am I being understood, or just read like an open book…”
“Itsuki-samaaa!”
“Ah, Rishia-san and the others are here too.”
“Motoyasu-sama! Welcome back!”
“Welcome back~”

Yuki-chan and Kou came running over, having heard the commotion. Itsuki was accompanied by Riska and the others. Ren’s Black Thunder was supposed to show up too, but hadn’t. Looking around, I spotted Kurotarou perched atop the roof of the hotel-slash-castle. Seemed to be a favorite spot. Ren noticed too, gazing up at the climbing Kurotarou from a distance.
“Anyway, let’s hurry up and solve the island’s mystery. Something tells me there’s another twist waiting ahead, but if we’re lucky, we might get back to normal right away.”
“So the idea is just to clear the dungeon that’s the prerequisite, and hope the only thing waiting after that is treasure.”

That was indeed true. If there turned out to be another hundred-floor dungeon, that would be a real pain, I say. Talking amongst ourselves like this, we arrived at the monument on the island where the hero-specific magic texts were inscribed. It was a bronze statue, like some sort of totem pole shaped from cultivation creatures. It looked like nothing more than a plain bronze statue, yet strangely, it showed no sign of rust despite years of wind and rain.
“…So, about that—we’re supposed to do a shoulder-stack here, right?”
“Yeah… seems like the order has to match the monument here too.”
“So Ren’s on the bottom, Itsuki on top of him, then Motoyasu-kun, and I’m on top.”
“Ah… guess that’s how it is.”
Ren stood in front of the totem pole, looking thoroughly unenthusiastic.
“A shoulder-stack, of all things. If Luna-san saw this scene, I wonder what face she’d make.”
“She’d probably be delighted.”

At that, I had the feeling that Father from the very first world, if left out of the loop, would be chuckling with amusement somewhere off to the side. Watching a fire from across the river sure is fun, isn’t it, Raphtalia—he’d probably say something like that, pointing at us. If it would make Father happy, then this Motoyasu shall happily oblige, indeed! Itsuki reluctantly began climbing up Ren’s body.
“There, now it’s Motoyasu-san’s turn.”
“Leave it to me, I say! Behold, the Usaunny Jump!”
I stomped the ground with all my might and leapt gloriously into the air! Landing on Itsuki’s shoulders with full force!
“A combination formation, I say! I believe this is called Pile-der On!”
I had a feeling that’s exactly the kind of thing Father would shout.
“Whoa!”
Wobbling, unable to bear the weight, Ren collapsed, sending Itsuki and me tumbling to the ground.
“Could you think just a little before acting?! Why would you leap on with full force?!”
“Ren, if you don’t put strength into your hips, there’s no way you can keep your balance, indeed.”
“My fault?! The cause was Motoyasu jumping with all his might and coming down like he meant to crush Itsuki flat!”
“If anything, it’s a miracle my body held up at all! That wasn’t landing, that was stomping! Motoyasu-san, are you trying to kill me?!”
Itsuki was being overly dramatic, indeed.
“Motoyasu-kun… or rather, this whole exchange is something we absolutely cannot show Luna-chan.”
“They’re supposed to be fighting, but… somehow, it feels oddly soothing.”
Fiancée seemed to be smiling faintly while looking slightly away.
“Really, it would’ve been nice if we could’ve filmed the heroes getting along so well on their journey, nano. It’d definitely be popular as a healing segment, nano.”
“It is absolutely not a healing segment or anything like that! My cheeks do not puff up!”
“Yuki-chan! If you dunk Itsuki in water, his cheeks puff up and he floats, indeed!”
“I simply must see that!”
Here I was, reporting the incidents discovered along our journey to Yuki-chan, indeed!
“Why do you keep exposing pointless things like that?!”
“Motoyasu, behave yourself!”
“In the first place, if we’re talking stability as a foundation, Naofumi-san is clearly the most suited, yet it’s irritating that he’s the one on top!”
“Well… even in this form, he’s still the Shield Hero, so among us he’s probably the sturdiest. The problem is that climbing to the very top looks like the hardest part.”
“Anyway, let’s just do this. Motoyasu-san, please just get on without doing anything strange.”
“I did nothing strange, indeed.”
I’d simply leapt on all at once, that’s all.
“Alright, Itsuki.”
“Right.”
Just as before, Itsuki climbed up onto Ren.
“Motoyasu, get on.”
“Understood.”
“Hey, why are—oof.”
Since Ren and Itsuki were being noisy, I climbed up, indeed. Using Ren’s face as a foothold, I scaled Itsuki’s body, hopped lightly onto his shoulders, and clamped his head between my feet.
“Gah—! Motoyasu-san, could you please ease up on the weight your feet are putting on my head?”
“Such a lot of demands, indeed.”
At that moment, Ren’s wobbling threw off the balance entirely.
“Ren, support us properly, I say!”
His weapon was strengthened and his level was more than sufficient—what was with this pathetic state, indeed?!
“Says the guy who stomped on my face. And stop wiggling around, Motoyasu!”
“Motoyasu-kun is being a complete nuisance…”
“Naofumi-san’s next. Motoyasu-san’s being annoying, so let’s hurry up and get this over with.”
“Y-yeah.”
And now it was Father’s turn. Looking rather timid, Father climbed up for us.
“Ah, my legs are too short, this is hard to climb…”
Since Father was a Peckul, his legs were the shortest among us, after all.
